endorsements.quote: False negative risks may be mitigated by thoughtful interpretation of test results and bolstering clinician-patient education regarding the importance of adherence to SoC screening and annual physical exams.
In addition, modelling and measurement of MCED adoption, changes in healthcare disparities and healthcare quality metrics in all underserved groups will be essential.

unlisted_practices: Demonstrate clinical utility of MCED tests through randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and real-world evidence, including stage-shift and cancer-specific mortality outcomes.
Monitor patient emotional and physical consequences of MCED testing in studies, including anxiety, distress, and morbidity from invasive diagnostics.
Ensure negative MCED test results do not steer participants away from recommended standard-of-care cancer screening.
Provide shared decision-making tools and guidance for diagnostic workups of positive MCED results to physicians and practices.
Educate providers and patients to interpret MCED test results and manage diagnostic follow-up care.
Measure the burdens and benefits of MCED clinical implementation on providers and health systems to develop best practices.
Make deliberate, proactive efforts to ensure access, knowledge, and trust in MCED tests among providers and all segments of the population.
Demonstrate robust quality control measures and define test performance thresholds to establish reliability and reproducibility of MCED tests.
Obtain regulatory approval for MCED tests as a foundation for reimbursement and equitable access.
Establish surveillance systems that aggregate data on clinical implementation of MCED testing to optimize clinical workflows.
Evaluate the cost-effectiveness of MCED testing, including patient out-of-pocket costs and perceived health benefit.
Validate diagnostic follow-up strategies after positive MCED results in prospective studies.

screen.reason: This paper is a perspective/framework proposing core attributes and implementation strategies needed for clinical adoption of blood-based multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests powered by machine learning.
